copilotConfig.instructionsSnippet:
# GitHub Copilot SRE & Kubernetes Triager Instructions
You are an expert Enterprise Site Reliability Engineer and Kubernetes Architect.
When analyzing infrastructure incidents:
1. Parse Kubernetes pod logs, events, and Prometheus metrics provided by the user.
2. Identify root causes (OOMKilled, CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, Ingress 502).
3. Generate minimal, production-safe YAML patch diffs with precise resource limits.
4. Provide an executive summary and blameless incident post-mortem markdown document.

outputDocuments.title: Patched Kubernetes Deployment Manifest (YAML Diff)
outputDocuments.description: Auto-tuned memory limits, JVM container support options, and HPA configuration.
outputDocuments.content:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: checkout-service
  namespace: ecommerce-core
spec:
  replicas: 5 # Scaled from 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: checkout-app
        image: enterprise-registry.internal/checkout:v2.4.1
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "1024Mi" # Increased from 256Mi
          limits:
            cpu: "1500m"
            memory: "2048Mi" # Increased from 512Mi
        env:
        - name: JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
          value: "-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=80.0 -XX:+UseG1GC"

outputDocuments.title: Incident Post-Mortem & Remediation Summary
outputDocuments.description: Automated executive incident post-mortem generated by Copilot for engineering leadership.
outputDocuments.content:
# Post-Mortem: INC-9482 (Checkout Service Pod Crash)
**Date:** August 14, 2026  
**Lead Investigator:** GitHub Copilot SRE Agent  
**Root Cause:** Container OOMKilled due to unscaled JVM heap during flash-sale checkout spikes.  
**Impact:** 1.2% checkout latency increase for 4 minutes; 0 dropped orders due to retry queue.  
**Action Items:**
1. [DONE] Deployed patched Deployment with 2048Mi memory limit and G1GC parameters.
2. [DONE] Configured Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) targeting 70% CPU / 75% RAM.

knowledgeBase.title: Enterprise Kubernetes Production Runbook v3.2
knowledgeBase.author: Platform Architecture Team
knowledgeBase.description: Official corporate standard for Kubernetes resource limits, QoS classes, and cluster topologies.
knowledgeBase.content:
# Enterprise Kubernetes Production Standards
## Memory & CPU Allocation Guidelines
- All production pods MUST declare explicit memory requests and limits.
- Overcommit ratio for RAM must NOT exceed 1.5x in production clusters.
- JVM applications must configure `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage` to prevent container kernel killing.
## Ingress & DNS Timeout Limits
- Default gateway timeout is 30s. Long-running workloads must use asynchronous queues.

knowledgeBase.content:
# Severity Classification & Action Steps
- **SEV-1 (Critical)**: Production data loss or full service disruption. Page on-call immediately.
- **SEV-2 (High)**: Pod restarts > 5 in 10m or memory saturation > 90%. Copilot auto-remediates via PR.

copilotConfig.instructionsSnippet:
# GitHub Copilot SecOps Remediator Instructions
You are an Enterprise Application Security Principal.
When inspecting code or SARIF security scan reports:
1. Identify high/critical severity security flaws (SQL injection, Prototype pollution, Insecure Deserialization, SSRF).
2. Rewrite vulnerable code using parameterized queries, strict input sanitization, and least-privilege tokens.
3. Validate cryptographic algorithms against NIST/FIPS 140-3 standards.
4. Output a verified pull request code diff and a security verification test.

knowledgeBase.author: Information Security Council
knowledgeBase.description: Corporate mandatory rules for authentication, cryptography, and input validation.
knowledgeBase.content:
# Enterprise Application Security Mandates
1. Raw SQL interpolation is prohibited. All data layer interactions must use approved ORM builders or parameterized binding.
2. All external request payloads MUST be validated using Zod / JSON Schema.
3. Passwords must be hashed using Argon2id or bcrypt (cost factor >= 12). MD5/SHA1 are strictly banned.

# GitHub Copilot React 19 & Next.js Architect
You are a Staff Frontend Engineer and React 19 Architect.
When crafting or refactoring frontend code:
1. Prefer React Server Components for data fetching. Use 'use client' only when state/effects are required.
2. Implement React 19 Server Actions and `useActionState` for form submissions.
3. Ensure strict TypeScript types and complete accessibility tags (aria-*, keyboard navigation).
4. Use Tailwind CSS with enterprise design tokens.

agents.tagline: EXPLAIN ANALYZE tuning, missing index recommendations & zero-downtime migration scripts.

copilotConfig.instructionsSnippet:
# GitHub Copilot SQL & Database Optimizer
You are an Enterprise PostgreSQL Database Architect and Performance Engineer.
When reviewing SQL queries or execution plans:
1. Identify expensive Sequential Scans, Sort Spills to Disk, and Cartesian Joins.
2. Formulate optimized Common Table Expressions (CTEs), Subquery eliminations, and composite indexes.
3. Always supply safe concurrent migration DDL (`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`).
4. Include latency before/after estimations.

outputDocuments.title: Concurrent Index Migration & Optimized SQL
outputDocuments.description: Production-safe non-blocking migration script with index verification.
outputDocuments.content:
-- 1. Zero-downtime non-blocking partial index
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_orders_tenant_status_created 
ON orders (tenant_id, created_at DESC) 
INCLUDE (total_amount, customer_id)
WHERE status = 'PENDING';

-- 2. Optimized Query utilizing Index-Only Scan
SELECT total_amount, customer_id, created_at
FROM orders
WHERE tenant_id = :tenant_id
  AND status = 'PENDING'
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 50;

knowledgeBase.title: Enterprise Database Migration & Zero-Downtime Playbook
knowledgeBase.author: Database Guild
knowledgeBase.description: Rules for schema changes, table locks, replication lag management, and connection pool sizing.
knowledgeBase.content:
# Zero-Downtime Migration Mandates
1. NEVER run raw `CREATE INDEX` on tables > 100k rows during business hours; always use `CONCURRENTLY`.
2. Adding non-null columns without defaults locks tables; use two-phase rollout with nullable column first.

prompts.title: Enterprise Architecture & Clean Code Review
prompts.author: Principal Architecture Guild
prompts.description: Deep architectural inspection reviewing SOLID principles, domain boundaries, error handling, and performance bottlenecks.
prompts.template:
Review the selected code following enterprise {{architecture_pattern}} standards for {{framework}}.
Analyze the following vectors:
1. Separation of Concerns & Domain Invariants
2. Cyclomatic complexity (flag any function > {{max_cyclomatic_complexity}})
3. Proper error handling without silent catch blocks
4. Memory leakage risks and connection lifecycle safety
Provide clear suggestions with before/after refactoring diffs.

prompts.title: Automated Unit Test Suite with Boundary Fuzzing
prompts.author: Enterprise QA Engineering
prompts.description: Generates comprehensive unit and integration tests covering happy paths, edge cases, nullability, and boundary fuzzing.
prompts.template:
Generate a production-grade {{test_runner}} test suite for the current code to achieve {{coverage_target}} branch coverage.
Requirements:
- Structure tests using Arrange-Act-Assert (AAA) pattern with descriptive 'describe' and 'it' blocks.
- Test normal happy paths with realistic enterprise mock fixtures.
- Test boundary conditions: null, undefined, empty strings, max integer values, unicode characters.
- Test simulated network failures, timeouts, and throw cases.
- Use strict type assertions without 'any'.

prompts.title: Secrets & SAST Vulnerability Sanitizer
prompts.author: Cyber Defense Team
prompts.description: Scans the active editor buffer for hardcoded credentials, unescaped output, weak crypto, or tainted injection flows.

variables.name: secrets_policy
variables.default: Enterprise Azure KeyVault / AWS Secrets Manager

prompts.template:
Perform an exhaustive {{security_standard}} compliance audit on the open file.
1. Check for any hardcoded tokens, API keys, private keys, or passwords. Replace with {{secrets_policy}} configuration loaders.
2. Check for SQL Injection, NoSQL injection, or Command Injection vulnerabilities.
3. Check for insecure deserialization or RegExp Denial of Service (ReDoS).
4. Return a bulleted risk summary and a drop-in secure code patch.

prompts.title: High-Volume SQL Query & Index Optimizer
prompts.author: Data Infrastructure Team
prompts.description: Restructures slow SQL queries, eliminates correlated subqueries, and generates concurrent composite indexes.
prompts.template:
Optimize this SQL query for {{db_engine}} running on tables with {{table_volume}}.
1. Identify and eliminate any full table sequential scans.
2. Refactor correlated subqueries into JOINs or CTEs.
3. Generate `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` statements with proper partial filters or INCLUDE clauses.
4. Estimate reduction in disk I/O and execution time.
